cards.heading: Sub-agent delegation: definition
cards.question: What is 'sub-agent delegation' as an agent architecture pattern?
cards.answer: A coordinating agent owns the workflow sequence, and specialized sub-agents each carry a focused instruction and narrow tool set; the coordinator transfers execution to a sub-agent at defined points, which completes its specialty, writes results to shared state, and hands control back.

cards.heading: Division of context, not labor
cards.question: Is sub-agent delegation best understood as a division of labor or a division of context?
cards.answer: A division of context: each sub-agent's instruction covers only its specialty and its tool list contains only what that specialty needs, unlike one monolithic prompt loaded with every tool and rule.

cards.heading: How sub-agents hand results back
cards.question: How do results produced by a sub-agent reach the coordinator and the rest of the workflow?
cards.answer: The sub-agent reads and writes the same shared session state as the coordinator, then hands control back — there is no separate result-passing channel.

cards.heading: Why delegation improves reasoning quality
cards.question: Why does splitting responsibilities into sub-agents improve reasoning quality compared to one monolithic prompt?
cards.answer: A single prompt carrying every tool description, workflow rule, and accumulated state degrades tool selection and step tracking, worse as context accrues in long-running work; narrow prompts keep each model call sharp regardless of total system complexity.
